source.title: Scalable and Accurate Self-supervised Multimodal Representation Learning without Aligned Video and Text Data
source.authors: V. Lialin; Stephen Rawls; David Chan; Shalini Ghosh; Anna Rumshisky; Wael Hamza

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a case where lower pretraining loss accompanies worse downstream performance, challenging the downstream-predictability version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites a scaling-law result but does not test power-law scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture invariance. Its pretraining-data comparisons report downstream captioning results, but do not vary model size, tokens, or compute to test scaling.
record.test_reason: The study cites Kaplan et al. once, for the idea that more data gives predictable gains, and never varies model size, tokens or compute. The crop-size remark compares training loss across two input resolutions with one fixed model and budget. Those losses are on different input distributions, so they are not comparable held-out losses, and no scale is varied. It is a different construct from V6, which concerns downstream gains predictable from scale or pretraining loss. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that captions from an image-captioning model work better than HowTo100M ASR captions for video pretraining. They also find that mixing images and videos gives the best result (+4 CIDEr on MSR-VTT), and they propose a separable cross-attention mechanism. They make no claim about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares crop resolutions and downstream captioning performance; it does not fit or evaluate scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Pretraining crop resolution changes the relationship observed between training loss and MSR-VTT performance.

fits_no_version.finding: A 320px-crop pretrained adapter model is reported to reach lower training loss than a 224px-crop model. The 320px model still does worse on MSR-VTT captioning throughout training. Separately, β2=0.95 models trained for 10K+ steps are reported to underperform β2=0.999 models trained for 4K steps downstream, despite lower pretraining loss. No numbers are given for either.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across training-setup choices at a fixed model scale (input resolution, optimizer β2), lower pretraining loss does not necessarily predict better downstream fine-tuning performance.

record.peer_reviewed: 2023 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
record.problems: The relevant loss-to-downstream comparison is qualitative, with no loss values, captioning scores, or uncertainty estimates stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Pretraining-data comparisons in Table 1 and crop-size results for fine-tuning resolution were not included because they do not test scaling, extrapolation, or the relation between pretraining loss and downstream performance.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5 challenge to V6 is not supported: the paper has no scale variation and no comparable held-out loss, and it reports only a qualitative anecdote. The β2 anecdote is also confounded by different step counts (10K+ vs 4K).

versions.untested_parts: The study uses image and video training but does not test whether loss follows a power law in those settings.
Scale-based predictability and a broader quantitative relation between pretraining loss and downstream performance.

rows.subject: OPT-1.3B and TimeSformer adapter-based captioning model
rows.stage_stated: pretraining followed by fine-tuning on MSR-VTT
rows.operation_detail: Compared models pretrained using 320x320 and 224x224 crops.

conditions.value: 320x320 vs 224x224; same batch size and number of update steps

rows.value: 320px crop network underperforms the 224px network consistently throughout training, despite having lower training loss
rows.locator: Section 6, “Effect of crop size during pre-training and fine-tuning”
rows.note: The comparison is reported qualitatively; no captioning score or training-loss value is given in the text.
rows.check: No scale is varied, and the two training losses come from different input resolutions, so they are not comparable held-out pretraining losses. The comparison is qualitative only, with no loss or CIDEr values. It does not measure V6's relation between scale or pretraining loss and downstream gains, so the link to V6 and the 'reversed' state should be dropped.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
